title: Fillets a la Orly

Sprinkle them well with lemon juice, pepper, salt, and parsley
Lay over them some slices of onion

Drain them for a few moments on kitchen paper

description: A sauce made with cheese, mullet or bream, and lemon juice.
steps: Fillet the fish, wash and dry them

Put a few little pieces of butter over them
Cover with buttered paper and bake from 20 minutes to half an hour, according to the thickness of the fillets
Place them carefully on the dish in which they are to be served

title: Fish a L'Aurore
description: Prepared with fish, onion, and white sauce.
steps: Put some dripping on a tin dish and lay the fish in it
Cover with a buttered paper and bake in the oven for twenty minutes
Take it out, split open and take out the centre bone
Sprinkle the inside of the fish with finely chopped onion and parsley, pepper, and salt
Put back the upper fillet and trim away some of the bones
Pour over the melted butter or white sauce
Put back into the oven for ten minutes
Boil the egg hard, remove the shell, take out the yolk and either chop it or rub it through a sieve
Cut the white into shapes
Take the fish from the oven and decorate the top with the yolk and white of egg

Dish them carefully, make the white sauce by recipe given, season it with pepper, salt, and half a teaspoonful of lemon juice.

title: Fish Cakes
description: A cake made with fish, potatoes, and fat.
steps: Free the fish from skin and bone and flake it up; mash the potatoes smoothly, mix together and season with pepper and salt.
Put the milk and butter into a saucepan, and when it is quite hot put in the fish and the potatoes.
Beat up the egg, and put half in, and mix together till hot through; spread on to a plate and stand away to cool.
Add a teaspoonful each of water and oil to the egg.
Make some bread crumbs on a sieve, and put them on to a piece of paper.
Shape the fish mixture into cakes about one inch high and two inches across; brush them over with the egg, and toss them into the crumbs.
Shape again and fry in very hot fat, arrange in the form of a wheel on a dish paper, garnish with fresh or fried parsley, and serve hot.

title: Fish Soup
description: A soup made with fish, fish stock, and cornflour.
steps: Remove all the fat from the fish stock and put it into a saucepan with six white peppercorns, an onion, one slice of turnip, a fagot of herbs, and some carrot.
Boil this together for twenty minutes, then strain out the vegetables and pour back into the saucepan.
Mix a tablespoonful of cornflour smoothly with the milk and stir it in; continue stirring till it boils.
Skin and fillet the fish and cut it into dice, put these pieces of fish into the soup, and simmer for ten minutes.
Just before serving add a few drops of lemon juice, and salt to taste.

title: Fish Stewed White
description: Prepared with fish, onion, and juice.

ingredients.name: the beaten yolks of four eggs

steps: Put an onion, finely chopped, into a stewpan, with a little oil, till the onion becomes brown
Add half a pint of water, and place the fish in the stewpan, seasoning with pepper, salt, and mace, ground allspice, nutmeg, and ginger
Let it stew gently until the fish is done
Prepare the beaten yolks of four eggs, with the juice of two lemons, a tea-spoonful of flour, a table-spoonful of cold water, and a little saffron
Mix well in a cup, and pour it into the stewpan, stirring it carefully one way until it thickens
Balls should be thrown in about twenty minutes before serving
For the balls: Take a little of the fish, the liver and the roe, if there is any, beat it up finely with chopped parsley, and spread warm butter, crumbs of bread, and seasoning according to taste

steps: Fillet the fish, put the bones in a saucepan, and just cover them with water.

title: Fish, To Fry

steps: Wash fish well in cold water, but not soaked; dry in a cloth.
Mix on a plate a spoonful of flour, pepper, and salt.
Beat on another plate an egg, with a spoonful each of water and oil, and have plenty of dry fine crumbs on a sheet of paper.

Drop into the crumbs, shake them all over it; toss in the hands to shake all the loose crumbs off.

title: Flaky Crust
description: Prepared with lard, juice, and flour.
steps: Sift the flour into a basin, cut about one ounce of the lard into it with a knife, then mix into a paste with the water; it should be about the same consistency as the butter.
Roll it out evenly, and lay on it small pieces of the butter and lard, sprinkle with flour and roll into three; roll out again and proceed as before.
It is ready for use at once if required, but it is much improved by standing in a cool place for an hour.

description: Prepared with grapes, brandy, and isinglass.

ingredients.name: three pounds of loaf sugar per gallon of wine

title: Gravy Soup
description: A soup made with ham or bacon, beef, and onions.

ingredients.name: half a pound of ham or lean bacon

steps: Cut half a pound of ham, or the same quantity of lean bacon, into slices, and lay them at the bottom of a digester, with six pounds of lean beef, cut into pieces
Clean two onions, two turnips, and two carrots, and a head of celery, a few cloves, and a blade of mace
Cover the digester close, and set it over the fire
When the meat adheres to the bottom of the digester, turn it
When there is a brown glaze on the meat, cover with hot water
When coming to a boil, put in half a pint of cold water, take off the scum
Put in some more cold water, and again skim it
Set it aside to simmer for full three hours
When done, strain it through a tamis, turn it into a pan
When cold, take off the fat
If thick, it must be clarified with the whites of two eggs

title: Mayonnaise Sauce
description: A sauce made with mustard, vinegar, and olive oil.

ingredients.name: a salt-spoonful of ordinary dry mustard
about a tablespoonful of good vinegar
quite a teacupful of olive oil

steps: Break each egg by knocking its side midway between the two ends against the rim of the bowl.
Allow the greater part of the white of the egg to escape into a small vessel, as it is not required for the mayonnaise.
With the yolk in one half of the shell, pour away all the white remaining in the other half.
Dextrously turn the yolk into the latter emptied shell and then get rid of the white left in the half previously occupied by the yolk.
Slip the two yolks into the bowl and break up with a few stirs of the egg-whisk.
Place within the bowl about a salt-spoonful of the ordinary dry mustard and beat well up in a second or two.
Add about a tablespoonful of good vinegar, the whisk going vigorously to work, and thus blend well together egg yolk, dry mustard, and vinegar.
With the left hand, tilt up the salad bowl and hold a bottle of salad oil at the same time.
Keep the bottle inverted over the contents of the bowl in such a way as to allow only a drop or so of the oil to escape at a time.
As the oil drops, keep unceasingly plying the mixture with the whisk.
Continue adding oil, faster and faster, until the amber-looking sauce is ready.
After stirring in a sufficient quantity of pepper and salt, the mayonnaise is complete.

title: Nesselrode Pudding
description: A pudding made with chestnuts, syrup, and cream.
